Capital One. What's in your wallet? Terms of fly. Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
Thanksgiving in the U.S. is being marked by heavy rains, strong winds,
and potential flooding along much of the east and west coasts.
In New York City, NPR's Steve Kestenbaum says the weather is pushing back
this year's Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade to Saturday.
Macy's parade executive producer Will Koss said they couldn't take any chances.
While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed,
the safety of our participants and spectators
is and always will be our top priority.
The postponement has far-reaching impacts New York Mayor Zoran Mamdani.
I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences,
yet safety has to come first.
The parade involves over 11,000 participants, mostly volunteers,
including over 10 high school marching bands from across the country.
Organizers now have to figure out who can stay through Saturday
and how to pay for the added costs.
Steve Kestenbaum, NPR News, in New York.
A federal judge is blocking the Federal Communications Commission
from immediately reviewing the local TV licenses held by ABC
and its parent Walt Disney.
As NPR's David Falkenflick reports,
the judge says the FCC unconstitutionally retaliated against the network
in response to programming that angered President Trump.
ABC sued after the FCC announced that it would immediately review
all eight local TV broadcast licenses held by ABC and Disney.
The agency had previously launched inquiries into Disney's diversity practices
and into the ABC talk show The View.
Trump had repeatedly called for ABC to be punished for its news decisions
and for jabs at him by late-night comic Jimmy Kimmel.
U.S. District Court Judge Lauren Ali Khan called the threat existential
and said the FCC's actions served to chill broadcasters' free speech.
She accused FCC Chair Brendan Carr of taking, quote,
"Trump's rhetoric, as his marching orders," Carr did not return
NPR's request for comment.
David Falkenflick, NPR News.
Health officials in Vermont say they've confirmed
more than a dozen cases of measles.
Vermont Public's Lola DeFord says these are the first cases of measles
in the Green Mountain State in decades.
Until recently, measles cases were extraordinarily rare in Vermont.
But Vermont State epidemiologist Emily Masaitis says,
with vaccination rates declining and the virus making a comeback nationally,
things were bound to change.
I think it shows that we are in such a different place
than we were, you know, 15 years ago, 20 years ago.
The confirmed cases all involve members of connected households
who weren't vaccinated against measles
and had recently traveled to another state with an outbreak.
Health officials are urging all Vermonters to check their vaccination status.
For NPR News, I'm Lola DeFord in Montpelier.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Duran Duran's original guitarist, Andy Taylor,
has died following about with prostate cancer.
He was 65.
NPR's Isabelle Gomez-Sarmiento says Taylor and the British band
first made their mark on pop rock music during the 1980s.
The year was 1980, and the ad in Melody Maker Music Magazine
sought out a "live wire guitarist" for a band.
A young Andy Taylor auditions for the gig,
and just a few years later, the music of Duran Duran
would become a global sensation.
Duran Duran became a fixture of the newly formed MTV,
and their new wave synth-heavy sound became a staple of the 80s.
Andy Taylor and his bandmates parted ways later that decade,
but they would reunite years later.
By 2022, Taylor was too sick to join Duran Duran
for its Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction,
but in a shared statement, his bandmates wrote of his remarkable courage, honesty, and grace.
Isabelle Gomez-Sarmiento, NPR News.
Authorities in Egypt say more than 30 people have been killed
in a fiery vehicle crash near Cairo.
It involved a tanker truck and dozens of other vehicles on a major highway surrounding the capital.
Video from the scene shows firefighters pulling people from burning cars.
More than two dozen cars and motorcycles were described as being charred.
Long flight delays were reported at Miami's airport last night
after a FedEx cargo plane overran a runway.
Nobody was injured.
This came about three months after an Amazon cargo jet overshot a runway,
leaving five people dead.
I'm Dave Mattingly in Washington.
the day.

topics.text: Thanksgiving weather forces Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade in New York to move to Saturday
Federal judge blocks FCC from immediately reviewing ABC and Disney local TV broadcast licenses
Vermont health officials confirm more than a dozen measles cases, first in the state in decades
Andy Taylor, original guitarist of Duran Duran, dies at age 65 after prostate cancer
Fiery vehicle crash on highway near Cairo, Egypt kills more than 30 people
FedEx cargo plane overruns runway at Miami airport, causing flight delays with no injuries
